name: Ascorbic acid
text:
Ascorbic acid is vitamin C. It occurs naturally in fruit and vegetables, and the food additive is usually produced industrially.

It is used as an antioxidant to slow browning and spoilage, for example in juices, canned fruit, cured meat and flour improvers.

It is approved in the EU with conditions and approved in the UK and the US.

name: Sodium ascorbate
text:
Sodium ascorbate is the sodium salt of ascorbic acid (vitamin C), made industrially. It is less acidic than ascorbic acid itself.

It works as an antioxidant that protects colour and flavour, and is common in cured meats and some drinks.

It is approved in the EU with conditions, and approved in the UK and the US.

name: Calcium ascorbate
text:
Calcium ascorbate is the calcium salt of ascorbic acid (vitamin C) and is produced industrially.

It is used as an antioxidant to prevent oxidation and discolouration in foods such as processed meat and some fruit products.

It is approved in the EU with conditions, and approved in the UK and the US.

name: Potassium ascorbate
text:
Potassium ascorbate is the potassium salt of ascorbic acid (vitamin C). It is an antioxidant by function and is not widely used in foods.

It is not approved in the EU, the UK or the US.

name: Fatty acid esters of ascorbic acid
text:
These are esters of ascorbic acid (vitamin C) with fatty acids, including ascorbyl palmitate. They are made synthetically. Unlike plain ascorbic acid they dissolve in fats.

They are used as antioxidants in fats and oils and in products containing them, helping to prevent rancidity.

They are approved in the EU with conditions, and approved in the UK and the US.

name: Ascorbyl stearate
text:
Ascorbyl stearate is an ester of ascorbic acid (vitamin C) and stearic acid, made synthetically. It is fat-soluble.

It acts as an antioxidant, mainly to protect fats and oils from rancidity.

It is not approved in the EU and the UK, but is approved in the US.

name: Tocopherol-rich extracts
text:
Tocopherol-rich extracts are natural mixtures of tocopherols (vitamin E), usually obtained from vegetable oils such as soybean oil.

They are used as fat-soluble antioxidants to stop oils and fatty foods from going rancid, and also serve as a source of vitamin E.

They are approved in the EU for certain fats and oils and for foods for infants and young children, and in the UK and the US.

name: Alpha-tocopherol
text:
Alpha-tocopherol is the most active form of vitamin E. The additive is the synthetic form.

It is used as an antioxidant to protect fats and oils from rancidity.

It is approved in the EU for certain fats and oils and for foods for infants and young children, and in the UK. In the US it is approved for inhibiting nitrosamine formation and in pump-cured bacon.

name: Gamma-tocopherol
text:
Gamma-tocopherol is one of the tocopherols, a form of vitamin E. The additive is the synthetic form.

It serves as an antioxidant, protecting fats and oils from oxidation.

It is approved in the EU for certain fats and oils and for foods for infants and young children, and in the UK. In the US it is approved for inhibiting nitrosamine formation and in pump-cured bacon.

name: Delta-tocopherol
text:
Delta-tocopherol is one of the tocopherols, a form of vitamin E. The additive is the synthetic form.

It is used as an antioxidant to slow the oxidation of fats and oils.

It is approved in the EU for certain fats and oils and for foods for infants and young children, and in the UK. In the US it is approved for inhibiting nitrosamine formation and in pump-cured bacon.

name: Propyl gallate
text:
Propyl gallate is a synthetic ester of gallic acid and propanol.

It is used as an antioxidant to delay rancidity in fats, oils, fried foods, snacks and chewing gum, often together with BHA and BHT.

It is approved in the EU with conditions, and approved in the UK and the US.

name: Octyl gallate
text:
Octyl gallate is a synthetic ester of gallic acid and octanol, used as an antioxidant in fats and oils.

It is not approved in the EU, where it was removed in 2018, nor in the UK. It is approved in the US.

name: Dodecyl gallate
text:
Dodecyl gallate is a synthetic ester of gallic acid and dodecanol (lauryl alcohol), used as an antioxidant in fats and oils.

It is not approved in the EU, where it was removed in 2018, nor in the UK. It is approved in the US.

name: Ethyl gallate
text:
Ethyl gallate is a synthetic ester of gallic acid and ethanol. It has antioxidant properties and is rarely used in food.

It is not approved in the EU, the UK or the US.

name: Guaiac resin
text:
Guaiac resin is a natural resin obtained from the wood of guaiacum trees.

It has been used as an antioxidant to protect fats and oils from rancidity.

It is not approved in the EU and the UK, but is approved in the US.

name: Erythorbic acid
text:
Erythorbic acid is a stereoisomer of ascorbic acid (vitamin C), produced industrially from sugars. It has little vitamin C activity.

It is used as an antioxidant, mostly in cured meat and fish products, where it helps keep colour and speeds curing.

It is approved in the EU in certain fish and meat products, and in the UK and the US.

name: Sodium erythorbate
text:
Sodium erythorbate is the sodium salt of erythorbic acid, an isomer of ascorbic acid, and is produced industrially.

It is used as an antioxidant in cured meat, sausages and some fish products, where it helps preserve colour.

It is approved in the EU in certain fish and meat products, and in the UK and the US.

name: Erythorbin acid
text:
Erythorbin acid is an obscure antioxidant related to erythorbic acid and is not used in common foods.

It is not approved in the EU, the UK or the US.

name: Calcium erythorbin
text:
Calcium erythorbin is an obscure antioxidant, apparently a calcium salt related to erythorbic acid. It is not used in common foods.

It is not approved in the EU, the UK or the US.

name: TBHQ
text:
Tert-butylhydroquinone (TBHQ) is a synthetic antioxidant made from petroleum-derived chemicals.

It is used to prevent oxidation of unsaturated oils and fats, for example in frying oils, snacks and instant noodles.

It is approved in the EU with conditions, and approved in the UK and the US. Its use is limited to small amounts set by regulators.

name: BHA
text:
Butylated hydroxyanisole (BHA) is a synthetic antioxidant.

It is added to fats, oils, snack foods, cereals, chewing gum and packaging materials to delay rancidity and extend shelf life. It is often combined with BHT.

It is approved in the EU with conditions, approved in the UK, and approved in the US with conditions. Regulators limit the amounts that may be used.

name: BHT
text:
Butylated hydroxytoluene (BHT) is a synthetic, fat-soluble antioxidant.

It is used to slow rancidity in fats, oils, snack foods, breakfast cereals and chewing gum, and is often used together with BHA.

It is approved in the EU with conditions, approved in the UK, and approved in the US with conditions. Regulators set maximum levels for its use.

name: Lecithin
text:
Lecithin is a natural mixture of phospholipids, obtained mainly from soybeans, sunflower seeds or egg yolk.

It is used as an emulsifier that helps oils and water mix, and is common in chocolate, margarine, baked goods and instant powders. It also has some antioxidant effect.

It is approved in the EU with conditions, approved in the UK, and approved in the US with conditions. Soy- or egg-derived lecithin may matter to people with those allergies.

name: Anoxomer
text:
Anoxomer is a synthetic polymeric antioxidant, an uncommon additive that is not widely used in food.

It is not approved in the EU and the UK, but is approved in the US.

name: Ethoxyquin
text:
Ethoxyquin is a synthetic antioxidant, best known as a preservative in animal feed and for protecting the colour of spices.

It is not approved in the EU and the UK. In the US it is approved for chili powder, paprika and, with conditions, in animal feed.

name: Sodium lactate
text:
Sodium lactate is the sodium salt of lactic acid, which is typically produced by fermenting sugars.

It is used as an acidity regulator and flavour enhancer, and is common in meat and poultry products, where it also helps extend shelf life.

It is approved in the EU with conditions, approved in the UK, and approved in the US with conditions.

name: Potassium lactate
text:
Potassium lactate is the potassium salt of lactic acid, usually made from fermented sugars.

It is used as an acidity regulator and antioxidant, particularly in meat and poultry products, where it also helps extend shelf life.

It is approved in the EU with conditions, approved in the UK, and approved in the US with conditions.

name: Calcium lactate
text:
Calcium lactate is the calcium salt of lactic acid, usually produced by fermentation.

It is used as an acidity regulator and firming agent, for example in canned fruit and vegetables, and as a source of calcium in some foods and drinks.

It is approved in the EU with conditions, approved in the UK, and approved in the US with conditions.

name: Ammonium lactate
text:
Ammonium lactate is the ammonium salt of lactic acid and functions as an acidity regulator. It is rarely used in food.

It is not approved in the EU, the UK or the US.

name: Magnesium lactate
text:
Magnesium lactate is the magnesium salt of lactic acid and functions as an acidity regulator. It is rarely used in food.

It is not approved in the EU, the UK or the US.

name: Citric acid
text:
Citric acid is an organic acid found naturally in citrus fruits. For food use it is produced mainly by fermenting sugars with the mould Aspergillus niger.

It gives a sour taste and regulates acidity in soft drinks, sweets, jams, canned foods and dairy products, and also helps preserve colour and flavour.

It is approved in the EU with conditions, approved in the UK, and approved in the US.

name: Sodium citrates
text:
Sodium citrates are the sodium salts of citric acid: mono-, di- and trisodium citrate. They are produced industrially from citric acid.

They act as acidity regulators and emulsifying salts, for example in processed cheese, soft drinks, jams and sweets.

They are approved in the EU with conditions, approved in the UK, and approved in the US.

name: Potassium citrates
text:
Potassium citrates are the potassium salts of citric acid: mono- and tripotassium citrate. They are produced industrially from citric acid.

They are used as acidity regulators and buffering agents in drinks, jams, dairy desserts and processed foods.

They are approved in the EU with conditions, approved in the UK, and approved in the US.

name: Calcium citrates
text:
Calcium citrates are the calcium salts of citric acid: mono-, di- and tricalcium citrate. They are produced industrially.

They serve as acidity regulators, firming agents and sequestrants, for instance in canned vegetables and fruit, and as a calcium source in fortified products.

They are approved in the EU with conditions, approved in the UK, and approved in the US.

name: Tartaric acid
text:
Tartaric acid is an organic acid found naturally in grapes and other fruit. The food additive is the L(+) form, usually obtained as a by-product of winemaking.

It gives a sharp, sour taste and is used in soft drinks, sweets, baking powder, jams and wine.

It is approved in the EU with conditions, approved in the UK, and approved in the US.

name: Sodium tartrates
text:
Sodium tartrates are sodium salts of tartaric acid: mono- and disodium tartrate.

They are used as acidity regulators and sequestrants in a limited range of foods.

They are approved in the EU for canned fruit and vegetables, biscuits, rusks and baby foods, and in the UK and the US.

name: Potassium tartrates
text:
Potassium tartrates are potassium salts of tartaric acid. Monopotassium tartrate is known as cream of tartar and forms naturally as a deposit during winemaking.

They act as acidity regulators and stabilisers, and cream of tartar is used in baking powder and to stabilise whipped egg whites.

They are approved in the EU for sweeteners, canned fruit and vegetables, biscuits, rusks and baby foods, in the UK, and in the US with conditions.

name: Sodium potassium tartrate
text:
Sodium potassium tartrate, also known as Rochelle salt, is a double salt of tartaric acid. Tartaric acid comes naturally from grapes.

It is used as an acidity regulator and sequestrant in a few foods.

It is approved in the EU for canned fruit and vegetables only, in the UK, and in the US for jams and cheese.

name: Phosphoric acid
text:
Phosphoric acid is an inorganic acid made industrially from phosphate rock.

It is used to give a sharp, tangy taste and to regulate acidity, most notably in cola drinks, and also in some processed foods.

It is approved in the EU with conditions, approved in the UK, and approved in the US. High total phosphate intake from all sources is a topic of nutritional discussion.

name: Sodium phosphates
text:
Sodium phosphates are sodium salts of phosphoric acid: mono-, di- and trisodium phosphate. They are made industrially.

They are best known as buffering agents, emulsifying salts and raising agents, used in processed cheese, meat products and baked goods.

They are approved in the EU with conditions, in the UK and in the US.

name: Potassium phosphates
text:
Potassium phosphates are potassium salts of phosphoric acid: mono-, di- and tripotassium phosphate. They are made industrially.

They are used as buffers, emulsifying salts and sequestrants in processed foods, drinks and dairy products.

They are approved in the EU with conditions, in the UK and in the US.

name: Calcium phosphates
text:
Calcium phosphates are calcium salts of phosphoric acid: mono-, di- and tricalcium phosphate. They are made industrially, and also occur in nature as minerals and in bone.

They are used as anti-caking and firming agents, in powdered products, baking powder and as calcium supplements in fortified foods.

They are approved in the EU with conditions, approved in the UK, and approved in the US.

name: Ammonium phosphates
text:
Ammonium phosphates are ammonium salts of phosphoric acid: mono- and diammonium phosphate. They are made industrially and are also known as fertiliser ingredients.

They are not approved in the EU and the UK, but are approved in the US.

name: Magnesium phosphates
text:
Magnesium phosphates are magnesium salts of phosphoric acid: mono- and dimagnesium phosphate, made industrially.

They are used as anti-caking agents.

They are approved in the EU with conditions, in the UK and in the US. The additive is also under discussion and may be included in a future amendment to the EU directive on miscellaneous additives.

name: Lecithin citrate
text:
Lecithin citrate is a derivative of lecithin treated with citric acid. It is a rarely used acidity regulator.

It is not approved in the EU, the UK or the US.

name: Magnesium citrate
text:
Magnesium citrate is the magnesium salt of citric acid. As a food additive it functions as an acidity regulator. It is also known as a dietary mineral supplement.

It is not approved in the EU, the UK or the US.

name: Ammonium malate
text:
Ammonium malate is the ammonium salt of malic acid and functions as an acidity regulator. It is rarely used in food.

It is not approved in the EU, the UK or the US.

name: Sodium malates
text:
Sodium malates are sodium salts of malic acid, the acid that gives apples their tart taste: sodium malate and sodium hydrogen malate.

They are used as acidity regulators.

They are approved in the EU for jams and jellies only and in the UK, but not in the US.

name: Potassium malate
text:
Potassium malate is the potassium salt of malic acid, an acid found naturally in many fruits. It is made industrially.

It is used as an acidity regulator.

It is approved in the EU and the UK, and not approved in the US.

name: Calcium malates
text:
Calcium malates are calcium salts of malic acid, an acid found naturally in many fruits: calcium malate and calcium hydrogen malate.

They are used as acidity regulators.

They are approved in the EU and the UK, and not approved in the US.

name: Metatartaric acid
text:
Metatartaric acid is a polymer-like product made by heating tartaric acid, which comes from grapes.

It is used in wine to prevent the formation of tartrate crystals.

It is approved in the EU for certain wines only and in the UK, but not in the US.

name: Calcium tartrate
text:
Calcium tartrate is the calcium salt of tartaric acid. It occurs naturally in grapes and as a deposit in wine.

It is rarely encountered in everyday foods.

It is approved in the EU with conditions and in the UK, but not in the US.

name: Adipic acid
text:
Adipic acid is a synthetic organic acid, produced industrially and used mainly to make nylon. It is also found in trace amounts in nature.

In food it acts as an acidity regulator and gives a tart taste in powdered drinks, gelatin desserts and jams.

It is approved in the EU with conditions, approved in the UK, and approved in the US with conditions.

name: Sodium adipate
text:
Sodium adipate is the sodium salt of adipic acid, a synthetic organic acid. It is used as an acidity regulator.

It is approved in the EU with conditions and approved in the UK. It is not approved in the US.

name: Potassium adipate
text:
Potassium adipate is the potassium salt of adipic acid, a synthetic organic acid. It is used as an acidity regulator.

It is approved in the EU with conditions and approved in the UK. It is not approved in the US.

name: Ammonium adipate
text:
Ammonium adipate is the ammonium salt of adipic acid and functions as an acidity regulator. It is rarely used in food.

It is not approved in the EU, the UK or the US.

name: Succinic acid
text:
Succinic acid is an organic acid that occurs naturally in many plants and in the body. For industrial use it is produced chemically or by fermentation.

It is used as an acidity regulator and flavour enhancer with a slightly salty-sour taste, for example in dry mixes and seasonings.

It is approved in the EU with conditions, approved in the UK, and approved in the US in condiments, relishes and meat products.

name: Monosodium fumarate
text:
Monosodium fumarate is the sodium salt of fumaric acid, an organic acid found in plants. It functions as an acidity regulator.

It is not approved in the EU and the UK, but is approved in the US.

name: Potassium fumarate
text:
Potassium fumarate is the potassium salt of fumaric acid, an organic acid found in plants. It functions as an acidity regulator.

It is not approved in the EU and the UK, but is approved in the US.

name: Calcium fumarate
text:
Calcium fumarate is the calcium salt of fumaric acid, an organic acid found in plants. It functions as an acidity regulator.

It is not approved in the EU and the UK, but is approved in the US.

name: Ammonium fumarate
text:
Ammonium fumarate is the ammonium salt of fumaric acid and functions as an acidity regulator. It is rarely used in food.

It is not approved in the EU, the UK or the US.

name: 1,4-Heptonolactone
text:
1,4-Heptonolactone is a lactone, a cyclic ester derived from a sugar acid. It is listed as an acidity regulator and is rarely used.

It is not approved in the EU, the UK or the US.

name: Niacin
text:
Niacin, also called nicotinic acid, is vitamin B3. It occurs naturally in meat, fish, grains and nuts and is also made synthetically.

In food it is mainly used to fortify products such as flour and cereals.

It is not approved as an additive in the EU and the UK, but is approved in the US.

name: Triammonium citrate
text:
Triammonium citrate is the ammonium salt of citric acid, made industrially. It is used as an acidity regulator.

It is approved in the EU in edible caseinates, in the UK, and in the US in condiments, relishes and meat products.

name: Ammonium ferric citrate
text:
Ammonium ferric citrate is a complex salt of iron, ammonium and citric acid. It is listed as an acidity regulator and can also serve as an iron source.

It is not approved in the EU and the UK, but is approved in the US.

name: Calcium glycerylphosphate
text:
Calcium glycerylphosphate is a calcium salt of glycerophosphoric acid, listed as an acidity regulator and used as a source of calcium and phosphorus.

It is not approved in the EU and the UK. In the US it is approved as a nutrient supplement or in gelatins, puddings and fillings.

name: Isopropyl citrate
text:
Isopropyl citrate is a mixture of esters of citric acid and isopropyl alcohol, made synthetically.

It is used as an acidity regulator. It is not approved in the EU and the UK. In the US it is approved in fats, oils, margarine and non-alcoholic beverages.

name: Calcium disodium EDTA
text:
Calcium disodium EDTA is a synthetic salt of ethylenediaminetetraacetic acid. It binds metal ions, which would otherwise speed up spoilage.

It is used as a sequestrant to protect colour, flavour and stability in products such as canned vegetables, sauces and dressings.

It is approved in the EU with conditions, approved in the UK, and approved in the US with conditions.

name: Disodium EDTA
text:
Disodium EDTA is a synthetic salt of ethylenediaminetetraacetic acid. It binds metal ions and is used as a sequestrant.

It is not approved in the EU and the UK. In the US it is approved with conditions.

name: Oxystearin
text:
Oxystearin is a mixture of glycerides of stearic and other fatty acids, produced industrially. It acts as a stabiliser.

It is used in vegetable oils to prevent crystals from forming at low temperatures.

It is not approved in the EU and the UK. In the US it is approved in vegetable oils.

name: Thiodipropionic acid
text:
Thiodipropionic acid is a synthetic compound used as an antioxidant.

It is not approved in the EU and the UK, but is approved in the US.

name: Dilauryl thiodipropionate
text:
Dilauryl thiodipropionate is a synthetic ester of thiodipropionic acid and lauryl alcohol. Substances of this type are generally used as antioxidants in fats.

It is not approved in the EU and the UK, but is approved in the US.

name: Distearyl thiodipropionate
text:
Distearyl thiodipropionate is a synthetic ester of thiodipropionic acid and stearyl alcohol. Substances of this type are generally used as antioxidants in fats.

It is not approved in the EU, the UK or the US.

name: Phytic acid
text:
Phytic acid is a natural compound found in the seeds of cereals, legumes and nuts, where it stores phosphorus. It can bind minerals such as iron and zinc.

It is not approved in the EU, the UK or the US.

name: Rosemary extract
text:
Rosemary extract is a natural extract of the herb rosemary. Its antioxidant activity is mainly due to carnosic acid and related compounds.

It is used as a natural antioxidant to protect fats, oils, meat products and snacks from rancidity.

It is approved in the EU with conditions, approved in the UK, and approved in the US.

name: Calcium lactobionate
text:
Calcium lactobionate is the calcium salt of lactobionic acid, which is derived from lactose (milk sugar).

It is used as a firming agent.

It is not approved in the EU and the UK. In the US it is approved in dry pudding mixes.
